test_title: PYST 79: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: If (3(16³ - 6³))/(16² + 6² + Q) = 30, then find the value of Q.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression follows the identity: a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Substitute a = 16 and b = 6, yielding a − b = 10 and ab = 16 × 6 = 96.

The numerator becomes 3 × 10 × (16² + 6² + 96) = 30(16² + 6² + 96).

Given the RHS is 30, the denominator (16² + 6² + Q) must be equal to (16² + 6² + 96).

By direct comparison, Q = 96.

**∴ The correct answer is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

[3(16³ − 6³)] ÷ (16² + 6² + Q) = 30

**Formula Used:**

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + b² + ab)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 16³ − 6³ = (16 − 6)(16² + 6² + 16 × 6)

⇒ 16³ − 6³ = 10(16² + 6² + 96)

⇒ [3 × 10(16² + 6² + 96)] ÷ (16² + 6² + Q) = 30

⇒ 30(16² + 6² + 96) ÷ (16² + 6² + Q) = 30

⇒ 16² + 6² + 96 = 16² + 6² + Q

⇒ Q = 96

**∴ The correct answer is 96.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). The middle term of the trinomial factor is always negative.

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). This is highly useful for simplifying numerators and denominators.

Algebraic Expansions

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
